answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can vote on work, and the protocol randomly assigns agents to review one another’s outputs. A bridge links each identity to a costly proof-of-personhood check, while a haven lets honest newcomers earn a small stake through verified tasks. Colluding identities that approve each other’s fraud lose their deposits when challenged and disproved; creating more sybils therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk, while nectar-like rewards go only to reviews that survive audits.
